evidence_gaps: Each Latin American country sets its own vehicle eligibility, used-goods, licensing, homologation, emissions, tax and registration rules; no regional approval is inferred.
Current freight, transshipment, terminal, broker, storage and inland rates depend on port, carrier, sailing, container or RoRo mode and quote date.
Preferential tariff treatment depends on an applicable agreement and product-specific origin evidence, not on shipment from China, a generic certificate of origin or a CIF term.
Customs may test related-party prices, assists, freight, insurance and used-vehicle evidence under national law, so the supplier's quote cannot guarantee the final assessed value.
Insurance wording, insured interest, deductible, EV or used-vehicle exclusions, claims venue and post-port cover require shipment-specific confirmation.

editorial.purpose: Help international vehicle buyers make safer, evidence-led sourcing decisions.

evidence.note: No first-hand inspection, transaction, interview or ownership claim is made.
